provenance: cold review of M4, finding 2. parse_matrix keyed rows on `section.startswith(...)` plus an exact cell count, and asserted nothing about having found anything. Renaming a heading, adding a TC6 or an Owner column, or leaving one unbalanced fence made a section silently parse to zero entries — and support-matrix-cites-real-cases stayed GREEN on it, because bad_status iterates the rows it did not find and every surviving citation still resolves. The frontend then rendered a clean, authoritative, header-only table: an agent declaring no limitations at all. Watched red as three variants that parsed quietly instead of raising.

triage.note: this is the honesty artifact failing in the flattering direction, which is the one direction that must never be quiet (CLAUDE.md rule 4). The fix is loudness, not tolerance: an empty section raises, so the /support-matrix endpoint 500s and the page shows an error rather than an empty promise. Also fixed alongside: the citation checker built its set of known case ids from evals/*/*.json, which included evals/report/*.json, so a report filename like `20260816-192727-fast` was accepted as a valid case citation.
